name: nav-path-following-visual
description: Tests path following and stuck state with building obstacles

steps.description: Opens the Crew panel with ensurePanel rather than a bare toolbar click (#556): the toolbar tab toggles, so when a preceding step has already opened the panel a second click closes it and the hire button underneath reports zero size.

A third driller so the three offices go up one apiece (#556). Ordering a building is queued work now, and two drillers splitting three builds spend long enough on them to cross their own collapse threshold — a collapsing employee never attempts a path, so the stuck state this file exists to watch would never be reached.

Walls the pocket off from the north: a 2x2 management_office covering (0,6)-(1,7), which blocks both cells directly north of the pocket. Its footprint is dead flat at surface height 37 on seed 42's terrain, as are the other two below -- the whole x:0-2, z:8-11 shelf is one level, so this trap needs no help from the placement tolerance (#1008). #556: confirming a placement only queues a construction site; one of the three idle drillers walks over and builds each wall for real, and the waitUntil step below drives all three to completion before anyone is dispatched into the pocket.
Walls the pocket off from the south: covers (0,10)-(1,11), blocking both cells directly south of the pocket.

Closes the pocket's only remaining side: covers (1,8)-(2,9), blocking the two cells east of it. With the west side sealed by the x=0 world edge, the pocket (0,8)-(0,9) is now enclosed on all 8 directions -- Pathfinding.ts admits a diagonal step with no corner rule, so every diagonal out of the pocket ((1,7) and (1,10)) has to be blocked too, which the north and south walls already cover.

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556) -- the next step waits for all three walls to actually land before the pocket is genuinely sealed.

steps.description: Drive all three wall sites to completion (#556) -- the idle drillers do the walking and building.

Dispatches employee #1 INTO the sealed pocket, at (0,8). Every route into it fails -- the pocket is enclosed by the three walls above plus the x=0 world edge -- so after STUCK_THRESHOLD consecutive pathfinding failures employee #1 flips to the stuck state. #1022 inverted the trap this file used to run: it used to seal the (0,0) map corner around the driller who had just finished building the last wall and dispatch them OUT, which made the whole assertion hinge on that builder still standing inside the pocket when it closed -- and #1008's placement rule then refused all three corner footprints outright, since that corner sits on a hillside (spread 2 across (2,0)-(3,1)) and no map corner is both flat and on the drillers' own bench level. Walling off a pocket and pathing into it from outside proves the same enclosure through the same A* search, with nothing riding on where a builder happens to be standing. Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one... which left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`.
Every route into the pocket fails since (0,8)-(0,9) is fully enclosed -- after STUCK_THRESHOLD consecutive failures employee #1 flips to the stuck state.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.
Re-dispatched to the same sealed pocket as before (#556) -- still unreachable, so employee #1 stays stuck.

expect.note: Shortened 10 -> 5 ticks (#556): the crew now spends ~65 ticks building the three offices before this block, so Walt enters it with fatigue already at ~35 and collapses 13 ticks in — and a collapsed employee is not a stuck one. Ten more ticks would have measured the collapse rather than the walled-off route this file is about; five keeps the whole block inside the window where the route itself is what is failing.

Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.
Demolish all three walls -- the previously stuck agent should be able to reach (0,8) once the pocket is open again.
Advance ticks after demolition — the stuck agent should resume moving toward its destination.
